text:
omar: Heads-up — noticed a consistent ~12% throughput regression hitting MQA Llama-2-13B after the kernel auto-select change yesterday. Baseline was ~540 tok/s, now ~476 tok/s on the same batch mix. Reverting kernel selection returns to ~538 tok/s.

lia: Hmm, was that the change that enabled the new matmul tiling for gqa/mqa split?

omar: Yes. Repo commit 8f3a2b6 — it picks tiled GEMM for >num_kv_heads thresholds. The interesting part: profiler shows extra stalls in the KV gather + RoPE apply stage, not pure GEMM time. Looks like a phase/stride mismatch when heads are interleaved for MQA.

angela: Can you paste the profiler snippet? nvprof/rocprof output or our perf traces are fine.

omar: Pasted sample stack (trimmed):
```
KV_gather  22.3%
RoPE_apply 18.9%
MatMul_tiled 29.1%
Kernel_fallback_overhead 9.8%
Memory_wait 20%
```
And hw counters show higher L2 miss rate on the tiled kernel path.

pranay: That smells like cache-line layout divergence. MQA uses num_key_value_heads != num_attention_heads mapping which can flip contiguous KV dims. If tiled GEMM assumes head-major layout, you get strided loads -> more L2 thrash.

jen: We saw something similar with Mixtral earlier — RoPE scaling interacted poorly with packed KV dimension ordering. The phase shift causes extra masking work and misaligned prefetch.

sam: Quick config dump from the failing run: 
```
model: llama-2-13b-mqa
num_key_value_heads: 32
kv_dim_per_head: 64
rope_scale: 1.1
batch_size: 8
micro_batch: 2
kernel_policy: auto_tiled
```

omar: When we force kernel_policy: fallback_unified (the old non-tiled kernel) throughput returns. So it's definitely a layout + tiling mismatch, not arithmetic precision.

perf-bot: Automated profile (1719004462): Detected 18% increase in L2 misses and 11% increase in memory stall cycles on tiled GEMM path for MQA configs where num_kv_heads < num_attention_heads.

lia: Proposed short-term fix: add a kernel-selection guard that checks head layout compatibility (num_kv_heads divides num_attention_heads or kv_stride aligned). If mismatch, prefer unified kernel. Low-risk and should restore perf.

angela: Mid-term: consider a KV layout transform pass that reorders KV buffer to be tile-friendly on the fly for MQA cases. That will cost an extra copy but could enable tiled GEMM perf. Need to model tradeoffs: copy cost vs L2 miss savings.

pranay: Also test alternate batching heuristics: when rope_scale != 1.0 or num_kv_heads != head_count, prefer smaller per-device batches to reduce working set size. Our autoscaler/scheduler can pick this per-model.

jen: I can prototype a layout-repack that runs when (num_kv_heads * kv_dim_per_head) % tile_width != 0. Should add microbenchmarks: repack cost, tiled vs unified performance, and memory pressure.

omar: For immediate mitigation, I'm rolling a hotfix that pins kernel_policy: unified for all MQA Llama configs where num_kv_heads != num_attention_heads. Patching infra to do this at model-onboard time.

sam: Quick note: add a regression test to eng-runtime perf CI that runs MQA Llama config with rope_scale variants (0.9,1.0,1.1) and both num_kv_heads values to catch this.

perf-bot: Regression test request created: #perf-ci-5421.

angela: Thanks — please also add a lightweight telemetry metric (kv_kernel_choice, kv_repack_triggered) so we can observe frequency and region of hits in prod.

omar: Will do. I'll push the hotfix branch and the perf CI after lunch. If anyone can help with microbench harness for the repack proof-of-concept, ping me. :coffee:
